objective: Build and verify Book Burner 0.1 Capture Edition: a professional native iPhone application for high-speed physical book capture, photo inventorying, location tracking, and self-contained ZIP/CSV/JSON export.
definition_of_done:
Native iPhone app builds cleanly with strict Swift concurrency checking on Xcode macOS environment
High-speed capture loop operational: Scan ISBN -> Photograph front cover -> Auto-save -> Instantly reset to scanner without manual Save buttons or blocking dialogs
Permanent monotonic identifier (BB-XXXXXX) assigned to every physical copy, surviving restarts and never reused or collided
Support duplicate ISBNs as separate physical records with unique BB IDs
Support offline capture, metadata failure, and 'No ISBN / Can't Scan' path with recoverable records
Metadata enrichment via Google Books and Open Library running asynchronously behind a provider seam with local caching and fallback
Location tracking with inheritance across session and safe 'Unassigned' fallback
Undo Last Book safely cleans up record and image assets without reusing the BB ID
Two primary native sections: Capture and Books (performant list, native search, filtering, and vertically scrolling detail)
Collection export producing valid ZIP containing books.csv, books.json, photos/, and manifest.json with full character escaping and relative asset integrity
SwiftData versioned schema and migration tests passing
Automated domain and unit tests passing with mock/fixture provider data and separated barcode acquisition seam
Real iPhone physical acceptance script passed including 25-book test and messy ~50-book test (or flagged CODE COMPLETE, PHYSICAL ACCEPTANCE PENDING until executed)

hard_constraints.text: Authoritative builds and tests must execute on macOS using Xcode
Target iOS version must run on Matthew's physical iPhone; do not target unstable/beta OS unnecessarily
No API secrets, credentials, or private tokens committed to Git repository; use Secrets.xcconfig.example
Do not embed eBay application client secrets or scrapers into the iOS client binary
ISBN must not be used as primary entity identity; each physical copy receives a distinct BB ID
Image writes must be atomic (temp write -> verify -> move/rename to permanent location -> commit persistence)
Full-resolution image blobs must not be stored in SwiftData records; use app-managed files with relative paths
Capture loop must never block on metadata enrichment or network latency
No fatalError, forced unwrap, or unhandled crash reachable during standard capture/export/network failures

architecture_decisions.text: Structure code around Features (Capture, Books, BookDetail, Locations, Export), Domain (Books, Identification, Metadata, Research), Infrastructure (Persistence, Networking, Photos, Archiving), Integrations (GoogleBooks, OpenLibrary), and Shared utilities. Avoid unnecessary Redux/TCA ceremony or giant service containers.

Define BookMetadataProvider boundary. Map external Google Books and Open Library DTOs to domain models without exposing provider schemas to the rest of the application. Fallback: Google Books -> Open Library -> Needs review.

Store photos deterministically named (e.g. BB-000127-front.heic) in the app sandbox. Save relative paths in SwiftData BookPhoto entities. Allow multi-photo support per copy (front, copyright page, signature, dust jacket, printing line, other).
Wrap VisionKit/DataScannerViewController behind a seam that emits barcode events to allow unit and UI testing with fake scanner inputs.

Generate BookBurner-YYYY-MM-DD.zip containing UTF-8 escaped books.csv, rich versioned books.json, manifest.json, and the photos/ directory using native APIs or a single pinned, lightweight Swift Package for ZIP creation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unit tests verify ISBN-10/13 validation, monotonic BB ID generation without reuse, CSV/JSON serialization, and provider fallback logic using fixtures.
SwiftData schema migration tests pass without data loss or model corruption.
Exported ZIP archive contains matching row counts in CSV and JSON, valid relative photo file paths, and uncorrupted special characters/Unicode.
Physical iPhone acceptance script executed including camera permissions, torch, offline scan, duplicate ISBN, unreadable barcode, location switch, and Undo.
Successful completion of 25-book test followed by the messy ~50-book physical pile test without blocking freezes or app crashes.

important_context.text: Target user is Matthew scanning a large physical pile of books needing triage (sell, bundle, donate, keep).
The application is fundamentally a high-velocity physical capture and liquidation tool, not a Goodreads-style reading tracker.
Physical capture outranks the network: network availability or provider failure must never pause or degrade physical scanning ergonomics.
Market valuation and eBay Browse API research integrations are scheduled for v0.2 to prevent credential leakage in the client binary.

important_rationale.text: Separating BB ID from ISBN ensures multi-copy inventory is treated as distinct physical assets with independent photo evidence and location tracking.
Decoupling photo writes to the filesystem keeps SwiftData lean and performant during rapid image acquisitions.
Avoiding modal dialogs and save buttons maximizes physical ergonomics when processing large book piles with one hand.
